text:
maria: heads up — customer reported dashboards showing metrics from another org after we flipped the quota policy rollout. hit it twice in prod during canary, quick repro:

maria: 1) login as user A (org A) 2) open /console/dash/42 3) quickly switch to user B (org B) via quick-switch 4) dashboard shows rows from org A for ~30s

jonathan: can you paste the request+response headers and any cache keys from the logs?

maria: sanitized curl and excerpt from web-worker logs:
```
curl -H "X-Redwood-Org: org-b" /console/dash/42
# log: GET /console/dash/42 -> cache_hit key=dashboard:42:v19 worker=web-9
# notice headers: X-Redwood-Org=org-b but cache key has no org
```

lee: uhoh — looks like cache key generation lost the org header when we switched to cookie affinity. cache key is: `dashboard:{id}:v{etag}` (no org prefix). that means a cached payload from org A can be served to org B on the same worker.

anya: :eyes: we enabled route-affinity by session cookie last week to reduce cross-zone latency. didn't think about tenant-scoped caches.

prashant: telemetry traces show mixed org tags on a single span: `worker.web-9 -> cached-response` with org=org-a then org=org-b for subsequent requests. quota attribution may have been charged incorrectly.

sre-bot: Created incident INC-2023-0123 and alerted oncall.

maria: short mitigation: disabled cookie-affinity for /console/* routes and purged dashboard keys on redis shards for affected timeframe. also increased sampling on traces for console requests.

jonathan: root cause: routing affinity + cache key missing tenant context. fix is straightforward: include `org_id` in cache key and assert request-owner in cached payload metadata. will add telemetry asserts to detect cross-tenant reuse.

maria: can you do a hotfix PR? plan: patch, run unit/regression including quick-switch simulation, cut canary, then promote. also add migration to evict stale keys.

jonathan: PR opened (internal): r/1234. changes:
- cache key -> `dashboard:{org}:{id}:v{etag}`
- cached payload includes `__owner_org` header
- added e2e test that simulates back-to-back user switch
- telemetry alert: count(cache_hit and request.org != cached_owner) > 0 -> pager

deploy-bot: canary rollout started to canary-2 at 23:02 UTC

lee: also double-check quota attribution in the billing/control-plane: if cached response was served across orgs we may have incremented tokens against the wrong tenant. need a sweep to reconcile.

anya: yes — creating ticket to run quota-reconciliation for affected window and notify CS. we should also document rollout-UX caveat: route-affinity can interact with per-tenant caches.

prashant: note for the infra team: consider namespacing shared caches by tenant by default or require explicit opt-in for tenant-agnostic caches.

maria: monitoring looks stable after purge and hotfix canary. leaving incident in triage for 24h and will convert to postmortem if customers were hit. thanks, team. :heart:
